Simple Linear Regression    Definition

Simple Linear Regression




Simple Linear Regression is a statistical technique that uses one explanatory
variable X to predict the outcome of a dependent variable Y





            TA Group                                CUHK(SZ)                              September 23, 2024           4 / 18

Simple Linear Regression    Casual Interpretation

Ceteris paribus effect





     Holding other factors fixed, how y changes when x changes

    Zero Conditional Mean Independence: E(u|x) = E(u) = 0
           Implies:
         Cov(x, u) = E(xu) = 0
         E(y|x) = β0 + β1x + E(u|x) = β0 + β1x

Ordinary Least Square (OLS) Estimation    Derivation

Minimize the sum of squared residuals



Find (ˆβ0, ˆβ1) to minimize the sum of the squared residuals ˆu2i


                                     n
                       min            X ˆu2i                                                           ˆβ0, ˆβ1
                                          i=1

                               n
                  min          X(yi −ˆβ0 −ˆβ1xi)2                                               ˆβ0, ˆβ1
                                   i=1

Mathematical theorem: The partial derivatives of the extremum point of the
continuous differentiable function are 0.





            TA Group                                CUHK(SZ)                              September 23, 2024           7 / 18

Ordinary Least Square (OLS) Estimation    Derivation

Mathematical derivation



At the minimum point of the function L(ˆβ0, ˆβ1):
     ∂L = −2 Pni=1(yi −ˆβ0 −ˆβ1xi) = 0       ∂ˆβ0
     ∂L = −2 Pni=1 xi(yi −ˆβ0 −ˆβ1xi) = 0       ∂ˆβ1


we derive:

                  Pni=1(xi −x)(yi −y)                                    ˆβ1 =
                    Pni=1(xi −x)2

                                             ˆβ0 = y −ˆβ1x





            TA Group                                CUHK(SZ)                              September 23, 2024           8 / 18

Ordinary Least Square (OLS) Estimation    Derivation

The method of moment




For the population regression model, there are two population moment conditions
when the SLR. assumptions have been satisfied.

    E(u) = 0

    Cov(x, u) = E(xu) = 0
Choose the ˆβ0, ˆβ1 to solve the sample counterparts of above equations.

Then we have the first order conditions (F.O.C.):
    n−1 Pni=1(yi −ˆβ0 −ˆβ1xi) = 0
    n−1 Pni=1 xi(yi −ˆβ0 −ˆβ1xi) = 0


The estimation results are the same as the results of OLS estimation solved by the
algebraic method.

Ordinary Least Square (OLS) Estimation    Properties

Properties of OLS estimation




     Fitted(or predicted) values:ˆyi = ˆβ0 + ˆβ1xi
      Residuals:ˆui = yi −ˆyi
     Estimator:ˆβ1 = △x△ˆy
     Algebraic properties of OLS statistics:
      Pni=1 ˆui = 0
      Pni=1 xiˆui = 0
          point (x, y) is always on the OLS regression line





            TA Group                                CUHK(SZ)                              September 23, 2024          10 / 18

Ordinary Least Square (OLS) Estimation    Standard Assumptions

Assumptions SLR.1-SLR.4





SLR.1 (Linear in Parameters)
    y = β0 + β1x + u

SLR.2 (Random Sampling)
    random sample {(xi, yi) : i = 1, 2, ..., n}

SLR.3 (Sample Variation in the Explanatory Variable)
     xi, i = 1, 2, ..., n, are not all the same value
   Pni=1(xi −x)2 > 0
SLR.4 (Zero Conditional Mean)
    E(u|x) = 0

Unbiasedness of OLS



Theorem 2.1: Unbiasedness of OLS

     under SLR.1-SLR.4
     E(ˆβ1) = β1, E(ˆβ0) = β0

Expected value of ˆβ1
                = β1 + Pni=1 wiui       ˆβ1 = β1 + Pni=1(xi−x)uiSSTx
     E(ˆβ1) = β1 + Pni=1 E(wiui) = β1 + Pni=1 wiE(ui) = β1

Expected value of ˆβ0
       ˆβ0 = y −ˆβ1x = β0 + β1x + u −ˆβ1x = β0 + (β1 −ˆβ1)x + u
     E(ˆβ0) = β0 + E[(β1 −ˆβ1)x] + E(u) = β0

Goodness of fit    Statistical terms

SST,SSE,SSR




Total sum of squares(SST):
   SST ≡Pni=1(yi −y)2


Explained sum of squares (SSE):
   SSE ≡Pni=1(ˆyi −y)2


Residual sum of squares (SSR):
   SSR ≡Pni=1 ˆu2i


Property: SST=SSE+SSR





            TA Group                                CUHK(SZ)                              September 23, 2024          16 / 18

Goodness of fit    R-squared

R-squared(coefficient of determination)





Definition:

     the fraction of the sample variation in y that is explained by x.
    R2 ≡SSESST = 1 −SSRSST


Properties:
    0 ⩽R2 ⩽1
   SSE ⩽SST
